rule: common rejection reasons: "the game having heavy use of generative AI material"; "the game being _very_ short"; not English; non-differing mod; paid ads; microtransactions
claim: Page says nothing on completeness or in-development games; full criteria are in a linked Oversight handbook (not read). Three staff votes decide; deleted games can usually resubmit after fixing.

rule: operator (u/YhvrTheSecond): "no intention of banning games that were made with generative AI outright" but plans to raise acceptance requirements for vibe-coded games; "over half of the time when people very blatantly did use it they say they did not"
claim: Galaxy labels AI-component games with a transparency label; operator says they seem to perform worse than their subreddit counterparts. Commenters largely favour mandatory disclosure and filtering; some say AI use 'sets my expectations low'. Snapshot is a Dec 2025 capture of a post about 321 days old, so about Jan 2025.

rule: "We ask that you accurately tag your project if it contains materials produced by generative AI"; "it is okay to create works in progress, or temporary pages"; "Feel free to share Draft or Restricted pages"
claim: Games may be disclosed via AI Disclosure section (listed on AI Assisted browse page); enforcement strict for asset pages only. Draft/Restricted pages are shareable without appearing in browse/New Releases. First public publish puts page on Most Recent and cannot be redone, so polish first. Algorithmic game AI/procedural generation needs no tag.

rule: "Assets using generative AI, even if subsequently modified, must be tagged appropriately, or they will not appear in our browse pages"
claim: Nov 2024 rollout; mandatory for assets, games optional per press reports (which disagree on scope).

rule: Rule 1D: 30 days between new self-posts, posts must refer to playable content; Feedback Friday thread stays available in that month
claim: Second-hand from search summary of a mod post (undated). reddit.com fetch was refused by tool; full rules page not read. No AI rule found.

rule: Feedback Friday: "This thread is for people to post their works in progress, and for others to give (constructive) criticism and feedback."
claim: Weekly AutoModerator thread is the sanctioned place for works in progress; snapshot contains no 30-day or AI rule text.
Single itch.io commenter speculates a dev's posts vanished from the incremental subreddit after he posted about being removed from Steam for AI art; commenter admits it is speculation. Unverified.

rule: "Don't launch in Early Access without a playable game"; "Do not make specific promises about future events"; "Customers should be buying your game based on its current state, not on promises of a future"; "Early Access is not a way to crowdfund development"
claim: Early Access fits a playable alpha/beta released in pieces, but cannot sell future content.

rule: Content Survey AI disclosure: Pre-Generated (development-time art, code, sound) and Live-Generated (at runtime, with guardrails); much of the disclosure shown on the store page
claim: Disclosure required, not a ban; Valve reviews output like non-AI content. Press summary from Jan 2024 and later 2025 update; Steamworks page not read.

rule: "AI should empower, not shortcut."; be ready to share tools, prompts and iterations on request; "transparency is appreciated" (credit not mandatory); "Games created (solely) with AI can create IP ownership issues."
claim: AI accepted if developer's own perspective is evident; heavy template/AI reliance may be declined; polish unfinished assets and resubmit after rejection. Quality guidelines list buggy/broken games as grounds for decline. Review 1-2 weeks (third-party).

rule: Two-step launch: Basic Launch then Full Launch (full visual QA, "Land directly in gameplay"); Quality Guidelines optional
claim: No AI rule on the page. Playgama (third party) says no AI label required. Basic Launch allows SDK-optional, no monetisation.
Third-party FAQ: CrazyGames public docs have no rule about AI-generated content; same review as other games.

rule: AI-generated art prohibited on the Art Portal (Sept 2022); some limited AI use allowed with notice
claim: Applies to Art Portal; I found no Games Portal AI policy text. Current policy not read from Newgrounds itself.
Fan wiki and a GDevelop page indicate Kongregate no longer accepts submissions; undated, unverified. Armor Games: no current submission rules found.
